clinicalPearls: Rare autosomal recessive organic aciduria caused by biallelic MLYCD variants encoding malonyl-CoA decarboxylase.
The biochemical hallmark is malonic aciduria in which malonic acid characteristically exceeds methylmalonic acid, with raised malonylcarnitine (C3-DC) on acylcarnitine profiling.
Cardiomyopathy, often dilated, is a characteristic and prognostically dominant feature that is unusual among the organic acidurias.
Neurodevelopmental delay, hypotonia and seizures are common, and developmental regression may occur.
Metabolic decompensation presents with hypoglycaemia, metabolic acidosis and ketosis, often with gastrointestinal symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal distension.
Malonyl-CoA is a key regulator of fatty-acid oxidation through inhibition of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1, so its accumulation disturbs cellular energy metabolism.
It may be detected on newborn screening through the elevated malonylcarnitine (C3-DC) marker.
reference.pathophysiology: MLYCD encodes malonyl-CoA decarboxylase, the enzyme that converts malonyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA and thereby sets the cellular concentration of malonyl-CoA. Malonyl-CoA is both a substrate for fatty-acid synthesis and a potent inhibitor of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1, the gatekeeper of mitochondrial long-chain fatty-acid oxidation. Enzyme deficiency causes malonyl-CoA to accumulate, and it is hydrolysed to malonic acid, producing malonic acidaemia and aciduria, while the raised malonyl-CoA suppresses fatty-acid oxidation; the combination of impaired fatty-acid oxidation and disordered malonate metabolism deprives the heart and brain of energy substrate and explains the cardiomyopathy and neurological features. Malonate additionally inhibits succinate dehydrogenase (mitochondrial complex II), contributing to secondary mitochondrial dysfunction.
additionalDifferentials: Combined malonic and methylmalonic aciduria (ACSF3 deficiency), the key sibling disorder, but there methylmalonate usually exceeds malonate
Classic methylmalonic acidaemias (MMUT and cobalamin-related defects)
Fatty-acid oxidation disorders, Barth syndrome and mitochondrial disease presenting with cardiomyopathy
Primary carnitine deficiency and other carnitine-cycle disorders
Glutaric aciduria and other organic acidurias presenting with encephalopathy
Malonate elevation secondary to other mitochondrial dysfunction
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids (malonate predominant over methylmalonate)
Echocardiography and ECG for cardiomyopathy surveillance
Molecular testing of MLYCD or an organic-aciduria gene panel
Blood glucose, gas, lactate and ketone measurement during illness
Enzyme assay in fibroblasts or leucocytes where available
redFlags: New or worsening heart failure from dilated cardiomyopathy
Acute metabolic decompensation with hypoglycaemia and acidosis during illness or fasting
Arrhythmia in the context of cardiomyopathy
Rapid neurological deterioration during catabolic stress
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is largely determined by the cardiomyopathy; with early diagnosis, avoidance of fasting, dietary measures and carnitine support some children do well, whereas progressive cardiac disease or severe decompensation carries significant risk.
pitfalls: Assuming malonic aciduria is always MLYCD deficiency, when combined malonic and methylmalonic aciduria (ACSF3) must be distinguished by the malonate-to-methylmalonate ratio.
Overlooking cardiac surveillance, since cardiomyopathy may dominate the outcome.
Attributing the dilated cardiomyopathy to a primary cardiac cause and missing the underlying metabolic diagnosis.
Under-recognising the risk of decompensation during fasting or intercurrent illness.
references: Physician's Guide to the Diagnosis, Treatment and Follow-up of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
Organic acidurias and fatty-acid metabolism reviews
management: Institute a low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet with strict avoidance of fasting and frequent feeds to reduce reliance on impaired long-chain fatty-acid oxidation
Supplement with L-carnitine to promote excretion of accumulated acyl-CoA species and correct secondary carnitine depletion
Provide an emergency regimen during intercurrent illness with increased carbohydrate intake or intravenous glucose to reverse catabolism and prevent decompensation
Treat acute metabolic decompensation with intravenous dextrose and fluids to correct hypoglycaemia and metabolic acidosis, temporarily withholding fat load
Undertake cardiac surveillance with serial echocardiography and ECG, treating dilated cardiomyopathy with standard heart-failure therapy
Support neurodevelopment with developmental assessment, physiotherapy and anticonvulsants for seizures
Coordinate care through a metabolic multidisciplinary team including metabolic physician, dietitian and cardiologist
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance and biallelic MLYCD variants, with testing of at-risk relatives
